question: Compare the average and median price_usd in the product prices dataset, then explain why they differ.
answer: The median, being the middle value, is less affected by outliers. citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR. Population variance divides the sum of squared deviations by N, the population size. Sample

citations.title: Statistics Robust Summaries
citations.text:
The mean is the sum of the values divided by their count, so every value, including extreme ones,
pulls it. The median is the middle value of the sorted data and ignores how far the extremes lie.
When a distribution is right-skewed (a long tail of a few very large values, as with prices or
incomes) a few large values drag the mean upward while the median stays near the typical value, so
the mean exceeds the median. When the data are symmetric the two are close. A large gap between the
mean and the median is therefore a quick diagnostic for skew or outliers. For skewed data, report
the median (or both) because it better describes a typical observation.

S5.title: Statistics Confusable Terms
S5.text: learning course). normal: the normal distribution is the bell curve. It does not mean "typical" or "healthy" values.  standardization: in this course standardization means converting values to z-scores with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. adjusted R squared: adjusted R2 = 1 - (1 - R2) * (n - 1) / (n - p - 1) where p is the number of predictors. Plain R2 never decreases when a predictor is added to the model, so adjusted R2 is used to compare models of different sizes. sample: in statistics a sample is a subset drawn from a population. In machine learning courses a sample often means a single row of data.
